supersedes.what_changed: the single LL target of v1 is replaced by a joint draw (SS, LL, TK | PI) with a supine conversion, a Roussouly shape rule, an in-field thoracolumbar coupling, an explicit rejection envelope and an envelope-covering fill-in; the cohort is now the grid re-measurement (one code path), not the release CSV

purpose: Per-level sampling distribution, junction rules and checks for generative use of the PolyPose polyrigid transform on labelled spine CT. The transform is published (Gopalakrishnan, Dey, Golland, NeurIPS 2025); only the sampling distribution, the junction rules and the checks are ours.

conventions.angle_sign: delta > 0 = more lordosis at that segment (extension direction); delta < 0 = less lordosis (flexion direction). Kyphosis-positive quantities (TLK) are reported with the opposite sign by measure_sagittal.py and converted at the boundary.
conventions.segment_naming: a segment is named upper-lower (L4-L5); its delta is the relative rotation of the upper body about the segment hinge with the lower body held.
conventions.hinge: centre of the intervertebral disc below the moving body: midpoint of the upper body's inferior plate centroid and the lower body's superior plate centroid, both from measure_sagittal.py (the release surface fit). Rotation axis = patient left-right axis (bicoxofemoral vector where femoral heads exist, else image x).
conventions.chain: absolute pose of body k = product of the relative hinge rotations of every mobile segment between k and the pelvis; the pelvis (sacrum, hips, femora, and any body fused to the sacrum) is the identity.
conventions.frame: analysis in the RAS canonical frame of nib.as_closest_canonical; volumes are never reoriented when written; axcodes are read and recorded.
conventions.label_ids: resolved with ostk.labels.labels_for(volume); the VerSe-native map (L1=20 ... L6=25, sacrum=26, T13=28, hips 30/31, femora 32/33) is required; id 29 is retired in v11 and never gated on.
conventions.frames: STANDING frame = the published normative cohorts; SUPINE frame = this cohort and every warped output; IMAGE frame = the CT with the pelvis fixed. PI is the same in all three (posture-invariant); LL, SS, TK are converted standing->supine with supine_conversion; PT and SS do not exist in the image frame beyond the pelvis' resting orientation on the table (see image_space_realisation).

conditional_given_PI.reading: at a given PI one degree of PI buys 0.63 deg of LL (Vialle 0.54, Hyun 0.62), 0.61 deg of SS (Vialle 0.54) and 0.10 deg of TK; the residual spread of LL around its PI-conditional mean is 9.0 deg, of SS 4.9 deg, of TK 10.9 deg

outside_checks_of_the_assembled_matrix.published_PT_regression: lafage2011 (PMID 21217459): PT predicted from PI, maximal LL and maximal TK, r = 0.93, SE 4.4 deg; coefficients quoted by secondary sources as PT = 1.14 + 0.71 PI - 0.52 LL - 0.19 TK and NOT verified from the paper; the assembled matrix gives 0.65 PI - 0.41 LL - 0.04 TK with residual 3.0 deg without having used it
outside_checks_of_the_assembled_matrix.reading: the matrix reproduces two published quantities it was not fitted to (PT and PI-LL spread) and lands near the ISSG PT predictor; it is assembled from four cohorts, not estimated on one, and the SS-TK entry is an assumption

compensation_slopes_at_fixed_PI.reading: loss of one degree of lordosis retroverts the pelvis by 0.43 deg on average (Lafage secondary-quoted -0.52; the vertical-trunk identity with TK ~ 0.45 LL gives -0.55; this cohort's unconditional SS-on-LL slope 0.56); the cascade of barrey2011 / diebo2015 (loss of LL -> PT up, SS down at fixed PI; thoracic hypokyphosis; knee flexion beyond) is the sign pattern of these slopes; knee flexion is outside the CT

balance_identity.reading: for a vertical trunk c is a constant plus the trunk's tilt; the published correlations give it an SD of 10.3 deg, far looser than the 3.1 deg SD of Vialle's T9 sagittal offset. The published matrix therefore does NOT encode a tight balance identity (TK definitions differ between series, cervical and T1 slope absorb the rest). The gate below uses the model's own band; a 3-degree identity would reject most of the literature's own cohort

supine_conversion.why: the normative cohorts stand; every CT here is supine; the sampler's targets and checks live in the supine frame
supine_conversion.sign_disagreement: LL: -4.6 (chevillotte2018, n=15, <50 y), 0 (fan2023, n=64, degenerative, MRI), +2.1 (bouaicha2014, n=52, trauma without fracture, CT), -6.2 at LL 55 (izatt2012, AIS adolescents, CT: LL_supine = 0.71 LL + 9.7), +11.3 (hasegawa2018, ASD, n=24). The direction is not consistent across series; the magnitude is a few degrees except in deformity

draw.note: one draw per output, recorded; SD chosen to span the published series; PI invariant (chevillotte2018 identical in all positions; hasegawa2018's -4.3 in ASD is a landmark effect and is not modelled)

cohort_check.reading: PI matches MEANS to 0.02 deg and Veilleux's automated supine CT to 0.07; SS is 6.6 deg below the supine model and PT 6.5 above it, which is the older, symptomatic, table-with-bolsters population effect documented in docs/SPINOPELVIC_ESTIMATOR.md (Hasegawa's older supine cohort: PI 53.4, SS 34.1, PT 19.2 within 2-4 deg of this one); LL is 3.8 deg below the supine model and its SD (14.0) is 1.24x the widest published (11.3): the cohort is wider than any normative series on both tails

image_space_realisation.pelvis: fixed in image space (pelvis_rule); PI, SS_image and PT_image are therefore INVARIANT by construction and re-measured as such (checks.pelvic_incidence)
image_space_realisation.PT_star_is_not_an_image_quantity: SS and PT are the pelvis' orientation against the vertical. With the pelvis held, the only image-space trace of a different standing PT* is the orientation of the trunk relative to the sacrum, which is the sum of the segmental angles: d(trunk vs sacrum) = dLL - dTK. So the pelvic-tilt compensation is realised by the segmental deltas themselves and by nothing else; a separate rigid rotation of the column on the sacrum would double-count it and would change the measured LL by the same amount. The task text's 'junction rotation IS the pelvic-tilt compensation' is honoured in this sense: the junction carries its share of dLL (zero when fused) and the drawn PT* is the standing tilt that the resulting relative geometry corresponds to, recorded in the manifest, checked through the balance gate, never applied as a rotation
what_is_applied: dLL over the mobile lumbar segments by the type-modulated shares (segment_share_of_LL)
dTLK_T10L1 = the in-field part of dTK over T10-T11, T11-T12, T12-L1 (thoracolumbar_coupling)
nothing on the pelvis, the sacrum, any fused body, or the femora

TLK_T10L2 / TL_T11L1 (must move by dTLK within tolerance)
junction angle (share x dLL; exactly 0 when fused)

joint_bounds.balance_residual: |c* - 19.5| <= 2.5 x 10.3 = 25.8 with c* = SS* - LL* + TK* (joint_sagittal_model.balance_identity)
joint_bounds.roussouly_consistency: the type assigned from SS* must be admissible for the drawn LL*: SS* < 35 with LL* > 70 or SS* > 45 with LL* < 40 is rejected (per-type LL means are not published with SDs in the sources on hand; these are the type-1/2 vs type-4 corners of the Roussouly table)

rejection_envelope.per_level: after distribution and one redistribution, the shortfall |dLL_shortfall| must be <= 3 deg and every segment inside its rom_deg cap x junction multiplier; otherwise the draw is rejected, not clipped further
rejection_envelope.source_plate_sanity: a source whose own measurement fails any of: LL in [10, 85], |junction disc angle| <= 30, |TLK_T10L2| <= 40, s1 plate accepted, PI available, is NOT a source (cohort_measurement.defects_found: 7 + 15 + 7 CTSP cases); a fused-junction source additionally needs its Castellvi read
rejection_envelope.after_warp: checks (below): re-measured LL within 2 deg of the request, TLK within 2 deg, PI/SS/PT within 0.5 deg, junction 0 when fused, Dice >= 0.98 per body, Jacobian > 0, body mask through the same field, DRR with a visible spine

fill_in_rule.goal: cover the WHOLE reference envelope, not only the thin bins: every anatomical profile the literature describes should exist in the bank
fill_in_rule.strata: PI bins of 5 deg from 25 to 80 (11 bins) x conditional-LL deciles (10) x Roussouly type implied by the draw -> targets drawn from the supine-converted conditional model within each stratum; strata are filled to a common count, so the low-lordosis and high-lordosis corners get as many outputs as the centre
fill_in_rule.source_choice: for each target (PI_bin, LL*): the source is drawn, seeded, uniformly among plate-sane ordinary cases with PI inside the bin and |LL* - LL_source_supine| <= 0.8 x the summed caps in that direction (38.7 flexion, 25.9 extension over five lumbar segments, v1); if none reaches, the nearest PI bin is tried once, then the target is recorded as unreachable
fill_in_rule.deficit_reading: which bins are 'thin' depends on the reference: against Chevillotte / Yukawa-shifted the cohort is short by 129-152 cases at LL 35-60 and long above 60; against MEANS-shifted it is short by 60 at 50-60 and long below 35. The three references disagree by 8 deg in the mean, so the fill-in covers the envelope uniformly by stratum instead of chasing one reference's deficit
fill_in_rule.rare_class_rule: for L6 / T13 / sacralised variants the target LL is drawn from the SAME reference distribution as ordinary spines (truncated at +/- 2.5 sd), so that lordosis does not separate the classes in the render bank. Rationale: 2-D angles separate LSTV from ordinary at AUC 0.78-0.83 in real life (albano2020), mostly through the fused junction; leaving that as-is would hand the network an angle shortcut for a decision that is a COUNT. PI, which the warp cannot change, keeps its real class association (yokoyama2016, haffer2021, jacob2023).

rare_class_profile_evidence.published: six-lumbar PI 64.8 vs 51.3 (yokoyama2016), 65.3 at true S1 (haffer2021); LSTV 58.5 vs 50 (jacob2023), 52.1 vs 47.8 (ouchida2024), 61.6 vs 50.5 (haffer2021); LL n.s. (yokoyama2016, jacob2023 +7); sacralisation measured at the first non-mobile plate 30.2 (muller2024) because the plate moves down one level (karabag2024: 27 deg between upper and lower plate)
rare_class_profile_evidence.reading: this cohort reproduces the literature: L6 PI 60.9 vs ordinary 52.0, sacralised 47.9. PI is where the class lives and the warp cannot touch it; LL* | PI is drawn from the same conditional for every class so lordosis does not become a shortcut

variants_per_case.rule: V warped variants per real rare CT, rendered at the same renders-per-CT as the source (200-500, ratio_report), so synthetic-anatomy : real-anatomy frames within the rare class = V : 1 <= 10 : 1 by construction; V chosen so that CTs carrying a variant are 25-35 % of rendered CTs: share = N_rare*(V+1) / (N_bank + N_rare*V)

V_full_bank.note: the cap binds; 25 % is reached only at V = 10 on the full bank

variants_per_case.film_level_caveat: against the 30 real L6 films (BUU) the existing physics_rare bank already holds 845 L6 crops (28:1), so a literal 10:1 per real rare film cannot be honoured without discarding renders; the real-film lever is the 4x epoch oversampling of those 30 films (ratio_report, VERIDAH), applied unchanged

ordinary_fillin_variants.rule: one variant per distinct ordinary source case, targets from the deficit histogram (total deficit 158.4 against the supine-shifted Yukawa reference); synthetic ordinary : real ordinary = 160 : 750 = 0.21

variants_per_case.arm_design: MEASURED ARM: train with and without the PolyPose variants at identical real-frame content and identical epoch counts; report per-class recall, PR-AUC and common-class precision on real held-out C-arm frames (body-box convention), paired bootstrap; the result is reported either way
variants_per_case.v2_counting_rule: CTs carrying a synthetic anatomy = rare variants (N_rare x V) + ordinary fill-in (N_fill); their share of rendered CTs must be 25-35 %; synthetic rare : real rare = V : 1 <= 10 : 1 by construction

renders_per_ct.source: ratio_report: SyntheX flattened at 250-500 renders per CT

corpus_size_estimate_full_bank.note: multiply by the number of device cards in the bank; the 20 TB volume holds ~25-40 card-corpora at this size; wall-clock is measured by the bank job, not estimated here

variants_per_case.warp_cost_estimate: PolyPose forward on a 512 x 512 x 600 grid: gravity-kernel EDT + per-voxel exp map, tens of seconds on one GPU plus the checks (Dice, Jacobian, DRR, re-measurement) ~1-2 min; 1,360 outputs x 3 seeds is a few GPU-days on one card and hours on 16 H200s; to be replaced by the measured number

target_LL.note: dLL_target = LL_target - LL_measured(source), with LL_measured from measure_sagittal.py on the unwarped volume (supine).

reference_supine_distribution.derivation: yukawa2017 standing 49.7 +/- 11.2 minus the 4.6 deg supine offset of chevillotte2018 (54.8 -> 50.2)

target_LL.posture_note: the C-arm frames are prone: prone on a Jackson/OSI frame equals or exceeds standing lordosis (peterson1995, lee2016 +5.3), the 90-90 / flexed-hip frames lose >35 % (peterson1995). The supine CT sits ~4.6 deg below standing. Targets therefore span the supine reference and its lordotic side, not a single posture.
target_LL.rare_class_rule: for L6 / T13 / sacralised variants the target LL is drawn from the SAME reference distribution as ordinary spines (truncated at +/- 2.5 sd), so that lordosis does not separate the classes in the render bank. Rationale: 2-D angles separate LSTV from ordinary at AUC 0.78-0.83 in real life (albano2020), mostly through the fused junction; leaving that as-is would hand the network an angle shortcut for a decision that is a COUNT. PI, which the warp cannot change, keeps its real class association (yokoyama2016, haffer2021, jacob2023).
target_LL.ordinary_fillin_rule: targets for ordinary spines are drawn from the per-5-degree DEFICIT histogram of the ordinary cohort against the reference (cohort_ctsp_release.json thin_bins_ordinary, to be superseded by cohort_grid.json); a source case is chosen, seeded, uniformly among ordinary cases whose measured LL lies within reach of the target (|LL_target - LL_source| <= 0.8 * sum of caps in that direction: 38.7 flexion, 25.9 extension over five lumbar segments) on the over-represented side of the target bin.

deficit_ordinary_vs_reference_supine_yuk.reading: the supine cohort is wider (sd 13.4) than any published series (9.6-11.3) with its excess above 60 deg; fill-in is on the LOW-lordosis side, 25-50 deg, which is also the flexed-frame intraoperative range

variants_per_case_ordinary_fillin.rule: one variant per distinct ordinary source case, targets from the deficit histogram (total deficit 158.4 against the supine-shifted Yukawa reference); synthetic ordinary : real ordinary = 160 : 750 = 0.21

per_vertebra_dice.rule: Dice(warped label_k, rigidly transformed original label_k) >= 0.98 for every k
per_vertebra_dice.note: nearest-neighbour resampling of a rigid motion is the noise floor

fused_junction.rule: relative motion of a body with multiplier 0 against the sacrum = 0: identical se(3) pose parameters, and re-measured junction angle change <= 0.25 deg

pelvic_incidence.rule: |PI_warped - PI_source| <= 0.5 deg; same for SS and PT

lordosis.rule: |dLL_measured - dLL_clipped_request| <= 2.0 deg (LL_L1S1_deg from measure_sagittal.py); noise floor: the same case measured on two label copies differing only in rib ids gave LL 43.83 vs 44.31 (0.5 deg)

thoracolumbar.rule: |dTLK_T10L1_measured - requested| <= 2.0 deg (TL_T11L1_deg and TLK_T10L2_deg from measure_sagittal.py, both must move in the requested direction)

wedge.rule: per-body wedge angle unchanged within 0.5 deg (rigid bodies)

body_mask.rule: SPINEPS body mask (tools/body_masks.py) warped through the same field, nearest neighbour; Dice(warped body mask, body mask re-run on the warped CT) reported, threshold 0.95

render.rule: one AP and one lateral DRR per output; bone term present (make_drr_dataset --paths2-only); the spine must be visible: bone-pixel fraction within the source's range and every vertebra's projected box non-empty

population.rule: over the generated set: KS test of supine LL, TLK and junction angle against the supine-converted model, per PI bin; the SD reported beside the model SD; the share of outputs in each Roussouly type reported beside laouissat2018 / shen2024

envelope_before_render.rule: rejection_envelope in full; the manifest row records every rejection and its reason

junction_share.rule: junction_angle_deg moves by share_L5S1(type*) x dLL within 2 deg; exactly 0 (<= 0.25 deg) when the multiplier is 0

source_sanity.rule: rejection_envelope.source_plate_sanity on the source row before any warp

what_is_not_known: no published series gives the per-type Roussouly LL mean with an SD; the type consistency gate uses table corners, not a distribution
the SS-TK correlation is not published as a pair and is set by assumption (0.35)
the Lafage 2011 PT coefficients were seen only in secondary quotations; the spec cites the abstract's r and SE and does not use the coefficients

no paper predicting LSTV from spinopelvic angles ALONE with a stated AUC was found; the closest is albano2020 (segmented lordotic angles on EOS, AUC 0.665-0.718 for type II, 0.797-0.831 for III-IV) and a 2025 deep-learning radiograph model (AUC 0.84, PMC12610351); geometry is weakly informative and the network must learn the count at the junction
no published segmental ROM exists for six-lumbar or thirteen-thoracic spines (v1 anchoring rule stands)
whether the standing coupling of TLK to LL should be imposed on a supine source at all: the cohort says it is absent supine
the T9 field-edge defect and the 29 disc/TLK/LL plate failures are excluded, not fixed
